Hi Sofia — great to hear from you and thanks for the requirements doc. I've sketched three recommendation buckets below based on the mix you described. Attached: SOW_v3.pdf and a concise pricing-comparison.xlsx that maps features to SKU lines.

1) Starter Predictable (hosted + limited reserved) — for smaller teams looking for cost predictability
   - Hosted API with reserved baseline throughput (monthly commit) + burst to shared capacity
   - Includes Optimize (basic) for batching/caching recommendations
   - Typical commitment: monthly or 6-months
   - Pricing example: ~$6k/mo baseline (usage overages billed at market rate)

2) Performance Dedicated (dedicated pool) — for mid-enterprise steady throughput with burst capacity
   - Dedicated GPU pool, SLA-backed latency targets, autoscale policies
   - Full Optimize + KV prefix caching enabled for low-latency chat endpoints
   - Optional private control plane integration (VPC) as an add-on
   - Pricing example: reserved baseline $20k/mo (with configurable burst credit bucket)

3) Enterprise Modular — full dedicated + private + advanced Optimize/observability pack
   - Annual commit recommended for deepest discounts and predictable unit economics
   - Includes rollout policies (canary), advanced tracing, longer log retention (add-on)

Discounting / downgrades / pilots notes:
- Standard pilot: 3-month Dedicated trial (baseline reserve + burst) — we can offer a pilot discount and migration credits (see attached SOW).
- Downgrade path: monthly commits are flexible; for annual commits we provide a stepdown schedule (pro-rated credits, 60-day notice) — I can outline exact stepdown math once you confirm baseline sizing.
- Pricing nuance: 12-month commit ~15% off list; 24-month ~25% off; pilot discounts typically 10% applied to reserved baseline.

Next steps I recommend:
- Quick 30-min call to review the SOW and pick a pilot configuration (I have slots Tue/Wed afternoon PT)
- I can generate an official quote and DocuSign-ready SOW once we agree baseline numbers

If helpful I can also run a small cost simulation for the workload you attached (estimate expected monthly token consumption and unit economics).

Thanks — cc'ing Marcus from Sales for contract/credit context.

Hi Sofia — looping in the commercial detail here. Short answers and some policy language you can use in procurement: 

- Downgrade (annual commit): We support a stepdown schedule with pro-rata credits and a 60-day notice. There is no punitive "termination" fee if you're converting to a lower reserved baseline within the same account, but credits applied to the account will be prorated based on unused reserved units. Example: If you commit $240k/year for baseline and step down halfway, we'll calculate unused monthly reserved portion and issue credit against future invoices.

- Conversion fee: We do not charge an explicit conversion fee for a stepdown; fees are limited to usage during the transition window if you require additional burst beyond remaining credits.

- Pilot overage: Pilot baseline includes a configurable burst credit bucket. Overage beyond burst during pilot is billed at agreed pilot overage rate (typically a blended rate lower than public list). We can cap monthly overage liability for procurement if needed.

- Feature mixing: Yes — you can split endpoints. Example config: chat endpoints on Dedicated (cached KV) + embeddings routed to Hosted. We support mixed routing rules and per-route billing lines so procurement can see discrete line items.

- Contract amendments: Add capacity mid-term via amendment with pro-rated charges for the remainder of the billing period. We'll attach amendment language in the SOW.

I'll coordinate with Hannah to produce the formal quote and updated SOW (with payment milestones and Net30 term callout).

Thanks,
